canonical_topic: Remote generation penalty and payment for deliverable power
definition: Under the SMD/LMP methodology, generators are paid based on the power actually delivered to customers (net of transmission line losses), not the gross power injected at the generation site.
core_idea: Historically generators were paid for gross power placed onto the grid regardless of location; because line losses reduce how much of that power actually reaches distant customers, LMP-based pricing instead pays generators only for deliverable power, creating a financial penalty for being far from demand.
key_points: Old model: generators paid for gross power injected at their site, ignoring transmission losses.
New (LMP) model: generators paid only for power that is actually deliverable to customers.
This creates an economic disincentive to build generation that can't effectively deliver power to load, and an incentive to build congestion-relieving transmission.
The combined effect (congestion allocation + remote generation penalty) is credited with improving overall grid reliability.
relationships: Second major component of FERC's Standard Market Design, alongside congestion cost allocation.
trading_implications: Plant siting decisions must weigh line-loss-driven revenue penalties for remote locations against fuel cost and efficiency advantages.
caveats: Being paid for 'power produced' is not the same as being paid for 'power delivered' under LMP — the distinction is the basis of the remote generation penalty.
